parts.text:
14 Which expression for pressure is correct?
A
force per unit area
B
force per unit volume
C
mass per unit area
D
mass per unit volume

hints: Look at the four word pairs in the options: force against mass, and area against volume - pressure must involve a push on a surface.
Recall the defining equation $p = F/A$ with $F$ normal to area $A$ and unit pascal $\text{Pa} = \text{N m}^{-2}$.
Compare mass per unit volume with the density equation $\rho = m/V$ to eliminate the density distractor, then check which remaining pairing gives $\text{N m}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Identify what is tested: the verbal definition of pressure using the words force, mass, area and volume.
State the governing rule: pressure is the normal force acting on a surface divided by the area of that surface, $p = F/A$.
Check units: force in $\text{N}$ divided by area in $\text{m}^2$ gives $\text{N m}^{-2}$, which is the pascal $\text{Pa}$, the unit of pressure.
Rule out the mass options: mass per unit volume is density, $\rho = m/V$, and mass per unit area contains no force so cannot make $\text{N m}^{-2}$.
Therefore only force per unit area matches both the equation and the unit. This is option A.

A.explanation: Pressure is defined by $p = F/A$, so force divided by the area it acts on.

B.explanation: Force per unit volume has units of $\text{N m}^{-3}$ and is not pressure.

C.explanation: Mass per unit area does not involve force, so it cannot give pressure in $\text{Pa}$.

D.explanation: Mass per unit volume is the definition of density, $\rho = m/V$, not pressure.
